question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
choice_b: A device that measures tire pressure on multi-trailer rigs
choice_c: A hydraulic jack used to raise the front of a trailer for hitching
choice_d: A type of parking brake found only on tank trailers
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Before backing a converter dolly under the rear trailer, what must be true of the trailer height?
choice_a: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_b: It must be raised as high as possible before coupling
choice_c: Trailer height does not matter for coupling
choice_d: It must be exactly level with the dolly frame
explanation: The manual states trailer height must be correct: it must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: After backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, how should you test the coupling before pulling out?
choice_a: Drive forward at low speed and brake hard
choice_b: Sound the horn and wait 30 seconds
choice_c: Release the parking brakes and check the mirrors only
choice_d: Pull against the pin of the second semitrailer
explanation: After backing the dolly under the rear trailer, the manual instructs drivers to test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: When making a visual check of a dolly-to-trailer coupling, what should you look for?
choice_a: That there is a small visible gap between the upper and lower fifth wheel
choice_b: That the safety chains are painted a reflective color
choice_c: That there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
choice_d: That the landing gear is fully lowered
explanation: The manual specifies a visual check should confirm no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel, with the locking jaws closed on the kingpin.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Why should you never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It voids the vehicle's manufacturer warranty
choice_b: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult
choice_c: It will trigger the trailer's anti-theft alarm
choice_d: It automatically drains all air from the trailer brake system
explanation: The manual warns never to unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of doubles, why should you lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer before pulling the dolly out?
choice_a: It is not necessary if the parking brakes are set
choice_b: To disconnect the electrical cord automatically
choice_c: To fully support the trailer and remove some weight from the dolly
choice_d: To make room for a spare tire
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly before uncoupling.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: Before disconnecting the dolly air and electric lines when uncoupling the rear trailer, what should you first do to the second trailer if it lacks spring brakes?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to chock the wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes, as part of the uncoupling procedure.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: What is the correct general order for coupling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Couple all three trailers together first, then attach the tractor
choice_b: Couple the third trailer to the tractor first
choice_c: Order does not matter as long as all connections are eventually made
choice_d: Couple the tractor to the first trailer, then use the converter dolly to couple the first trailer to the second trailer, and repeat for the third trailer
explanation: The manual describes coupling the tractor to the first trailer using the standard tractor-semitrailer method, then moving the converter dolly into position to couple the first trailer to the second trailer, using the same method for additional trailers.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When inspecting the upper and lower fifth wheel on a doubles/triples combination, the locking jaws should be closed around what part of the kingpin?
choice_a: The kingpin does not have locking jaws
choice_b: The shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_d: Either the head or the shank
explanation: During inspection, the manual specifies checking that the locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When inspecting the landing gear on a double or triple trailer combination, what should you confirm?
choice_a: That it matches the color of the tractor
choice_b: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, and is not bent or otherwise damaged
choice_c: That it has been recently painted
choice_d: That it is left partially lowered for stability while driving
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist requires landing gear to be fully raised, with no missing parts, and not bent or otherwise damaged, with the crank handle in place and secured.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: On a set of double or triple trailers, what should the shut-off valve position be at the rear of the front trailer(s) versus the rear of the last trailer?
choice_a: Rear of front trailer(s) should be CLOSED; rear of the last trailer should be OPEN
choice_b: Rear of front trailer(s) should be OPEN; rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED
explanation: The manual's inspection list states shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: During the tractor protection valve test, at what air pressure range should the trailer air supply control pop out to the emergency position?
choice_a: Only when the tank is completely empty of air
choice_b: Usually within the range of 60 to 80 psi
choice_d: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
explanation: The manual states the control should pop out when air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: What can happen if the tractor protection valve does not work properly?
choice_a: An air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to activate with possible loss of control
choice_b: It has no effect on braking performance
choice_c: The trailer lights will flicker but braking is unaffected
choice_d: The fifth wheel will automatically release
explanation: The manual warns that if the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly, an air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When testing trailer service brakes on a doubles/triples rig using the hand control (trolley valve), what confirms the brakes are working correctly?
choice_a: The trailer air supply knob pops out
choice_b: You should feel the brakes come on, confirming the trailer brakes are connected and working
choice_c: The dolly wheels lock immediately at any speed
choice_d: The tractor's parking brake releases automatically
explanation: The manual explains that applying trailer brakes with the hand control while moving forward slowly should produce a felt braking effect, confirming trailer brakes are connected and working.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4

question: How can you check that air flows all the way to the last trailer in a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Check the fuel gauge for a pressure drop
choice_b: Visually inspect the tires for wear patterns
choice_c: Rev the engine and listen for a whistling sound from the cab
choice_d: Push in the red trailer air supply knob, go to the rear of the rig, and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer to listen for escaping air
explanation: The manual describes pushing in the trailer air supply knob to charge the emergency lines, then going to the rear of the rig and opening the emergency line shut-off valve at the last trailer to confirm air is escaping, showing the system is charged.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4
